first_impression.reaction: Googled 'bali wedding venues' while comparing planners. The title says '15 Best', which makes me roll my eyes, but the intro straight away says 'The list runs by area, not by rank', so fine. The table with 'Not published' all down the exclusive-use column is the most honest thing I've seen on a venue list. Jumped to the FAQ: capacities, chapels, legal steps, all with numbers. What's missing is any money at all. Not one venue price, and nothing on what Wedded Wonderland charges or whether it takes a cut.

journey.quote: 15 Best Bali Wedding Venues From Clifftops to Beaches
journey.reaction: Best by what measure? The body itself says it isn't ranked. The headline is the only place that sounds like an ad.

journey.section: Bali wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: Good. They're telling me where the gaps are, not papering over them.

journey.quote: AYANA Bali runs one of the most varied wedding estates on the island, with an expert wedding team and dedicated planners who guide couples through details such as cake and florals with the resort's chefs and restaurants.
journey.reaction: 'One of the most varied' and 'expert wedding team' are the venue's own marketing, repeated. Whose words are these?

journey.quote: A 60-guest ceremony fits Tresna Chapel, but a seated dinner for the same group needs a second space, so plan the move between them into the timeline.
journey.reaction: Actual working-out from published figures. This is the trade-off a brochure wouldn't mention.

journey.quote: One couple featured in the resort's own wedding story married at the fountain and held their reception at Akasa.
journey.reaction: Admits the evidence is one wedding story. Thin, but honest about being thin.

journey.quote: Site visits are by appointment, and whether a minimum spend or rental fee applies depends on the space and the type of event.
journey.reaction: So there's a minimum spend or rental fee, amount unknown. That's the catch I'm looking for, and no figure anywhere on the page for any venue.

journey.quote: Grand Hyatt Bali hosts weddings from manicured gardens to a beachfront sanctuary, and claims the longest shoreline in the Nusa Dua area.
journey.reaction: 'Claims' is the right word. Attributes the boast to the hotel instead of repeating it as fact.
A product name, not a fact. What does it do and why does it matter for a wedding?

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: Use this table to narrow by guest numbers. Each figure is the venue's own, for the space named.
journey.reaction: This is the spreadsheet I'd have built myself. Sourced, sorted by headcount. Most useful part of the page.

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from capacity to exclusive use, needs an answer in writing before you commit, and your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you sign, through Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: Advice to get it in writing is right, and I got burned on exactly that. But this is where you'd tell me how your fee works, and you don't.

journey.section: Which part of Bali suits your wedding?
journey.quote: Before you decide, get a feel for Bali weddings in the pages of the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
journey.reaction: 'Get a feel' is mood, not evidence. Show me a real Bali wedding with the budget instead.

journey.section: When is the right time to get married in Bali?
journey.quote: Smartraveller's overall advice for Indonesia is to exercise a high degree of caution, and Bali falls under that overall level.
journey.reaction: A wedding business quoting the government advice level, plus methanol and rabies. Not hiding the downside. Trust up.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Bali?
journey.quote: Persons of any nationality may generally marry in Indonesia if they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government, listed as Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian, and both parties must hold the same religion.
journey.reaction: That's a real catch most venue lists skip, stated plainly with a source. Matters a lot for us.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Bali?
journey.quote: For specific requirements, including any fees, contact the nearest Indonesian Embassy or Consulate-General, or the Civil Registry Office (Catatan Sipil) where you will marry, and talk to a lawyer to confirm validity.
journey.reaction: Fees again pushed off the page. Fine for legal fees, but it fits a pattern: every dollar figure is somewhere else.

journey.section: Shortlist your Bali venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing is good. But 'payments' through you means money passes your hands. Do you take a cut from the venue? Not answered.

unanswered_questions: What does any of these venues cost? Even a published 'from' package price or minimum spend, with a date, for a few of the 15.
Which venues apply a minimum spend or venue hire fee, and roughly how much (Samabe says one may apply)?
Room counts for the resorts, so I know if 100 guests can actually stay on site.
Can a couple of different religions, or no religion, legally marry in Bali, or is a symbolic ceremony plus an Australian legal marriage the only route?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee calculated, and what's a realistic 'from AUD' for a Bali wedding? (deferred business detail)
Do you take commissions or mark-ups from these venues, and will you disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real Bali wedding you've planned, with the actual budget. (deferred business detail)
Have you worked with any of these 15 venues directly, or is this compiled from their websites? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: 15 Best Bali Wedding Venues From Clifftops to Beaches
turn_offs_found.why: 'Best' with no criteria, contradicted by the page itself saying the list isn't ranked. Unsupported claim in the first thing I see.

turn_offs_found.quote: AYANA Bali runs one of the most varied wedding estates on the island, with an expert wedding team and dedicated planners who guide couples through details such as cake and florals with the resort's chefs and restaurants.
turn_offs_found.why: Superlative and 'expert' repeated from venue marketing without attribution, unlike the careful 'claims' used for Grand Hyatt.

turn_offs_found.quote: Site visits are by appointment, and whether a minimum spend or rental fee applies depends on the space and the type of event.
turn_offs_found.why: Signals a cost exists without any number, and the whole page has no prices. Unquantified costs look like the catch.

turn_offs_found.quote: Before you decide, get a feel for Bali weddings in the pages of the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional nudge to a magazine instead of evidence like a real wedding with a budget.
Brand name dropped as a 'standout' with no fact behind it.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the guest-count table and the same-religion rule for a legal marriage in Indonesia
Our Reddit thread: the Smartraveller points (methanol, wet season October to April, buffer day for volcanic delays) and the 'get Not published answers in writing' advice

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, shortlist your Bali venues through Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: The page earned trust: sourced numbers, honest gaps, government warnings up front, and CTAs mostly sit after the evidence. But there's not a single price, and nothing on how you're paid or whether venues pay you. I'd email those two questions before booking a call.

top_3_changes: Add published cost signals where the source allows: any venue 'from' package price or minimum spend with an 'as at' date; where none exists, say 'pricing not published' in the at-a-glance table so the gap is explicit.
Drop 'Best' from the title or define the criteria, and attribute or cut the AYANA 'one of the most varied' and 'expert wedding team' lines the way Grand Hyatt's 'claims' is handled.

Near the Concierge CTA, state plainly how the fee works and whether supplier commissions apply (deferred business detail), and swap the 'get a feel' magazine line for a real Bali wedding with its budget if one exists.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and tables first, hunted for prices, fees and commissions, flagged superlatives and mood lines
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, real weddings and venue relationships listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold any published venue package prices, minimum spends or room counts? If yes, adding a few closes the cost objection; if not, an explicit 'pricing not published' column is the fallback.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'bali wedding venues' while comparing planners; relevance 4, enquiry 2 because no prices and no fee or commission model.
Business details (fees, commissions, real weddings, venue relationships) are deferred; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Rendered link text and bold labels quoted without markdown syntax, as a reader would see them.
Fast-mode read: intro, tables, FAQ, legal, safety and closing read closely; individual venue profiles skimmed.
